historical_reviews.v3_1: The Web label explicitly says BMC and server settings; scope must be proven before reset because assuming a BMC-only action could miss host-impacting defaults. Each temporary setting needs a documented expected factory default, not merely disappearance.

original_test_intent: Prove that the approved BMC factory-reset workflow removes known temporary configuration, restores DHCP networking and documented defaults, and allows secure management recovery.
original_method: On an isolated target, bind the exact Web reset action and affected BMC/server scope, export and hash supported configuration, establish console/PDU and DHCP discovery, apply/read back at least three owner-approved reversible changes including static IP, obtain final approval, issue one reset, discover the BMC at its new DHCP identity with bounded polling, rotate any factory credential, compare every changed field and the broader default matrix, then restore only required management configuration and verify BMC/server health.
manual_activity: The owner selects the isolated SUT, exact changes/defaults and reset scope and gives final go/no-go; an operator maintains console/PDU/DHCP recovery, rotates credentials and owns any restoration and verdict.
required_inputs: Vendor-supported Web/Redfish factory-reset action and BMC/server scope
At least three approved reversible setting changes with expected defaults
Static address, expected DHCP network and lease-discovery method
safety_requirements: Never reset an unisolated production BMC
Do not clear logs or destroy baseline before export
Verify exact target and reset scope from vendor documentation
Keep secrets out of commands and validate TLS/host identity
Read back every temporary change before final approval
Do not rely on the old static address after reset
Issue the factory reset once only and never retry automatically
Stop on missing backup, recovery, DHCP or credential-rotation capability
Preserve server/BMC evidence and unexpected impact
agent_execution_scope: Capture complete redacted BMC/server baseline and configuration hash
Apply/read back only approved temporary changes
Submit one factory reset after explicit final approval
Compare factory defaults and rotate credentials
Assist approved restoration and report evidence without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve reset action/scope and isolated maintenance window
Select temporary settings and expected defaults
Control credential rotation/restoration and decide PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The suggested Manager.Reset action may be unsupported for factory defaulting; `-k`, command-line passwords, fixed sleep and old-IP ping are unsafe and cannot prove the static-to-DHCP transition or configuration defaults.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-documented BMC Web/factory-reset action exactly once after backup and final approval, then discover the same hardware through DHCP/console, rotate credentials and compare the documented defaults and approved restoration.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: At least three changed items, static-to-DHCP behavior, Reset BMC and server settings and 15/15-minute estimates are retained; fixed timing or default credentials are not assumed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed change/default ledger covering identity, each temporary value, expected factory value, baseline export hash, reset response, DHCP lease/MAC correlation, credential rotation, observed defaults, approved restores and final health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a complete evidence/recovery chain around the destructive source workflow without weakening its reset or DHCP acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A BMC restart or ping response does not prove factory reset; the management address, accounts, certificates, policies and selected settings must match documented defaults, and server scope must be checked.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Reset can erase the only management path and may reset server-affecting policy; deleted configuration may be unrecoverable if vendor export/restore is incomplete.

project_override_considerations: The Project must state whether post-test configuration remains at factory default or is restored after evidence, and which server settings the Web action resets. Lack of a vendor-defined default or independent recovery is an execution stop, not permission to guess.
expected_evidence: Verified target, vendor action/scope/default matrix, maintenance approval, recovery proof and configuration export/hash
At least three temporary setting writes/readbacks including static IP and their expected defaults
Final approval and protected single reset request/response with bounded outage timeline
DHCP lease/MAC/console evidence binding the new address to the same BMC
Post-reset default comparison, secure credential rotation and BMC/server health
Approved restored settings, SEL/audit/host logs, recovery/no-secret record and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require a factory reset and static-to-DHCP default. The breadth of `BMC and server settings` and exact defaults are vendor/project inputs, not competing source instructions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Vendor reset semantics, default matrix, isolated target, configuration backup and independent recovery are normal critical-operation prerequisites; the objective is identifiable without guessing them.

review_improvement: Converts an unsafe one-line reset into a target-bound, backed-up and recoverable default-state proof that explicitly handles the management address and credentials that disappear during the test.
independent_technical_reasoning: A factory reset is demonstrated by state convergence to documented defaults, not by reboot completion. Since the old static route is expected to vanish, successful verification depends on an independent identity anchor such as BMC MAC plus console/DHCP lease correlation. The recovery plan must exist before mutation because the action can erase every credential and network path used by the automation itself.
